scenes.text: Seven a.m. You're unwell, so you go to the hospital. By the time a doctor sees you, it's almost noon.
Then you queue again: for the specialist, the lab, and the pharmacy. Referrals get lost, results travel on paper, and you pay before anyone helps you.
DocSpecialCare puts that whole journey online. No queues, no lost paperwork.

It runs on NEAR, a blockchain. Think of it as a fair digital referee. It holds your payment safely, keeps a permanent record of every step, and lets only the people you choose see your health information.
Meet Amaka. She has chest pains, so she picks a doctor and a time that suits her.
Her payment doesn't go straight to the doctor. NEAR holds it, and releases it only after the consultation. If the doctor doesn't show up, she gets it back.
At her appointment, she chats with the doctor and joins a private video call. Only the two of them can read it.
Doctor Tunde refers her to a heart specialist. The referral is recorded on NEAR, so it can't get lost. He completes the visit, and he's paid automatically.
Amaka books the specialist with her referral, who orders blood tests. She pays the lab the same safe way.
The lab locks her results before sending them. NEAR keeps only a fingerprint of the results, and a list of who may open them. The lab is paid on delivery.
The specialist opens them. This green check proves nothing was changed on the way.
She prescribes medicine. Amaka chooses a pharmacy, and only that pharmacy can read the prescription.
Amaka pays, and the medicine is handed over. Each prescription works only once, and any pharmacy can check it's genuine.
Every step you saw is a real transaction on NEAR. Each one confirms in about a second, for a tiny fraction of a cent.
Patients wait less and own their records. Doctors, labs and pharmacies get paid fairly. And everyone can trust the process.
DocSpecialCare. Care without the queue. Built on NEAR.
